prompt:
Extract every policy commitment stated in the text below.

Rules:
- One commitment per line.
- Write each as a verb phrase: an action followed by its object. For example: "raise the income tax threshold" or "build 300000 new homes".
- State each commitment at the level of a distinct policy action, not its implementation details. Do not subdivide a single commitment into steps.
- Include every commitment. Do not select, rank, prioritise, or judge importance.
- Use the text's own terms for policy objects. Do not substitute synonyms.
- Do not number the lines. No bullets, headings, preamble, or commentary.
- If the text states no policy commitments, output the single word NONE.

<text>
Conservative Party Manifesto 2015 — Summary (ideological framing preserved)

Our plan is to secure a better future for you and your family at every stage of life by sticking to a clear Conservative approach: a strong economy first; rewarding hard work; backing aspiration; protecting the vulnerable; and keeping our country safe.

Economy and tax
- Finish the job: eliminate the deficit, run a surplus and start paying down debt to keep taxes and mortgage rates low.
- No rises in VAT, Income Tax or National Insurance; raise the Personal Allowance to £12,500 and the 40p threshold to £50,000; new Tax‑Free Minimum Wage law.
- Crack down on tax evasion and aggressive avoidance; keep competitive business taxes and cut £10bn more red tape.
- Rebalance growth: build the Northern Powerhouse, devolve powers and business rates growth, and back elected metro mayors.
- Invest over £100bn in infrastructure: HS2/HS3, road upgrades, frozen commuter fares, universal broadband, better mobile and 5G.

Jobs, skills and business
- Create 2 million more jobs and achieve full employment.
- Deliver 3 million new apprenticeships; abolish long‑term youth unemployment with tougher Day One requirements and a time‑limited Youth Allowance.
- Support SMEs with a business rates review, Start Up Loans, prompt payment and a permanent Office of Tax Simplification.
- Invest in science, innovation and high‑value industries; boost the rural economy and champion British farming and fishing.

Fair welfare and family support
- Make work pay: lower the household benefit cap to £23,000; roll out Universal Credit; freeze working‑age benefits (with key exemptions).
- 30 hours of free childcare for working parents of 3–4 year‑olds; tax‑free childcare; back marriage with transferable allowances.

Controlled immigration
- Keep net migration to the tens of thousands by reforming EU welfare rules, enforcing exit checks, clamping down on illegal working and exploitation, introducing a Controlling Migration Fund, and requiring fluent English in public‑facing roles.

Education and opportunity
- Protect per‑pupil funding; zero tolerance of failure; tougher standards in literacy/numeracy; core academic GCSEs.
- Turn every failing/coasting school into an academy; open 500 new free schools; expand UTCs and Degree Apprenticeships.
- Lift the cap on university places; introduce postgraduate loans; maintain world‑class research.

NHS and social care
- Increase NHS spending every year; at least £8bn extra by 2020 to deliver a truly 7‑day NHS, same‑day GP appointments for over‑75s, named GPs, and digital access.
- Lead on cancer, mental health parity, dementia research; integrate health and social care; cap residential care costs.

Homes and ownership
- Double first‑time buyers; extend Help to Buy and introduce Help to Buy ISAs; build 200,000 Starter Homes at 20% discount for under‑40s.
- Extend Right to Buy to housing association tenants; prioritise brownfield; protect the Green Belt.

Law, security and justice
- Finish police reform; strengthen victims’ rights with a Victims’ Law; tackle extremism with new powers; reform prisons to cut reoffending.
- Scrap the Human Rights Act and introduce a British Bill of Rights.

Energy and environment
- Keep bills down through competition, smart meters and efficiency; back new nuclear, gas and promising renewables; halt new subsidies for onshore wind; support least‑cost carbon cuts.
- Protect nature with a UK and Overseas Territories Blue Belt; strengthen flood defences; plant 11 million more trees.

Culture, society and the Union
- Free entry to national museums; freeze the BBC licence fee; back creative industries and school sport; expand National Citizen Service and offer three days’ paid volunteering.
- Protect pensioners: triple lock, single‑tier pension, pension freedoms, retain key benefits; raise the effective Inheritance Tax threshold on the family home to £1m.
- Strengthen the Union: English votes for English laws; implement new powers for Scotland and Wales; support a stable, prosperous Northern Ireland.

Europe and the world
- Renegotiate Britain’s EU relationship and hold an in‑out referendum by end‑2017; keep the pound; reclaim powers; complete major trade deals.
- Maintain strong Armed Forces, renew Trident, meet NATO commitments; uphold 0.7% aid to tackle poverty, conflict and disease.

This is a disciplined, long‑term Conservative plan to reward work, back aspiration, protect vital services, and keep Britain strong, secure and free.
